admission.justification: Spans pyproject.toml and test_code_quality_check_scope.py, is proved by a live Pyright test, and prevents a [tool.pyright] exclude pattern from silently dropping tracked Python files from hook and wrapper file-list checks.

applicability: Explicit file-list Pyright invocations in .githooks/_gate.sh and quality_plan.py against root pyproject.toml.
conditions: Pyright runs with --project . and explicit Python file paths passed on the command line.

Every pattern in [tool.pyright] exclude remains disjoint from tracked Python files so [tool.pyright] exclude drops zero listed tracked files (Pyright 1.1.414+'s independent default **/.* exclude applies separately to dot-folders such as .dagger/).
exclusions: Bare Pyright invocations with no command-line file arguments, which resolve paths through [tool.pyright] include.
Untracked or ignored files under excluded environment, dependency, build, or cache directories, and Pyright 1.1.414+'s independent default **/.* dot-folder exclusion.

statement: A Pyright command-line file list replaces [tool.pyright] include while Pyright still filters listed files against [tool.pyright] exclude, so the hook (.githooks/_gate.sh) and quality wrapper (quality_plan.py) file-list runs report the exact same diagnostics before and after the change because zero tracked Python files match any [tool.pyright] exclude pattern (Pyright 1.1.414+'s own default **/.* exclude applies independently to dot-folders such as .dagger/).
title: Pyright CLI file lists replace include while exclude filters listed files
